findings.before_claim: require_admission requires the receipt's existing_gpu_count to be an integer in [1, 2], the spec's allocated_gpu_count to be an equal integer, and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to contain exactly that many distinct, nonempty entries. After preflight and before claim_once, main also requires torch.cuda.device_count() to equal the admitted count and rechecks the time and GPU budgets.
findings.before_fit: run_science enumerates CUDA again and compares the resulting lane-list length and the spec count with the count verified before the claim. That same list goes to core.lanes for fitting. A discrepancy at this second check raises before any fit starts.
findings.regression_coverage: By source inspection, test_integration.py expects ValueError for each requested case: a two-card receipt with a one-card spec and visibility ['0', '1'], duplicate visibility ['0', '0'], and a CUDA inventory of one against an admitted count of two. It also checks that matching counts of two are accepted. No tests were executed in this review.

risks: Native technical canary, observability and artifact proof, measured all-cost forecasts, and guarded launch review remain pending.

lifecycle_correctness.preclaim_failure: A count mismatch detected in main leaves the one-time campaign claim available.
lifecycle_correctness.postclaim_failure: A mismatch detected in run_science stops before fitting or qualification and leaves the campaign claim consumed.
lifecycle_correctness.gate_decision: Neither failure reaches gate_decision or emits a promotion decision. The R3 source verdict does not authorize launch.

confidence: High for the narrow F3 source verdict.
review_scope: stage/data and lifecycle supplied source, zero independent execution
